### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-record-context`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via getQueryableFields (literal, a string literal in security))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via getQueryableFields (literal, a string literal in security))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **188** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d8aa8a6e092741c53fcc15548446116eedd799a7` — the merge of head `88a1447c951570e533ee1cb7c4b21be8e44a5f53` into base `f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d8aa8a6e092741c53fcc15548446116eedd799a7 && git checkout d8aa8a6e092741c53fcc15548446116eedd799a7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729 88a1447c951570e533ee1cb7c4b21be8e44a5f53 && git checkout -B drift-repro f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729 && git merge --no-ff 88a1447c951570e533ee1cb7c4b21be8e44a5f53

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a50181d4e7d5b508fad66b05a45cd3141ed58e12`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts + packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/door.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/__tests__/record-context-tools.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts, .changeset/37361-record-context-left-out-queryable-doors.md
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #37412 (cards #37361 and #37175), reviewed read-only: both card threads whole, the PR body, the net diff against `main` (8 files, +483/-44), ADR-0160 on `main`, and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff (plugin-security, `query-read-limits.ts`, the two doors' existing members, `action-execution.ts`) was read, not reviewed.

Check-runs on the head: 58 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure once the newer run of a repeated name governs. `PR-body guards` was red at 02:37:14Z (closing target #37175 claimed by another branch) and is green at 03:15:44Z, after re-claim 7181502252. `Check Changeset` is green on both runs. `Check PR Size` and `Auto Label` read skipped on the 03:15 re-run and were green at 02:37.

### ① Derived judgments

- **A related child this caller is not served: refused whole before, left out now. Right.** ADR-0160 D3 "Object level" (amended 2026-11-25) says it in these words: "A `related` child that this caller is not served is left out … Nothing of the child is read, its definition included. Its section is not named." Step 4a adds the child to `leftOut`, sets `hidden`, and `publishedOf` answers `null` for it, so the plan, the projection, `withheldAmong`, `diagnoseDelegation` and the query never see it. Read for leaks: the answer carries no section, no row, no count and no field name of the child; the one note is `not_visible` with no `object` member. The service pin asserts the door was asked only `readGuard`, `assertApiExposed`, `servedObjectDefinitionOf` for the child, and that neither its name nor its label is in the serialized answer; the real-kernel pin asserts the same bytes on `/mcp` and stdio with a served control (`rc_revision`, row `r1` only, so row security still holds beside it).
- **Gate order read guard, then API exposure, then the served definition. Right.** D3 step 1 lists the three gates in that order. A child that is both unexposed and not served refuses unnamed, as before (`shown` is true only when the served definition is non-null, and a throw there reads as not shown). `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` is outside `API_EXPOSURE_REFUSALS`, so it refuses unnamed under `PERMISSION_DENIED`, the one code point 12 gives. A served-definition read that throws now refuses unnamed where it used to fall into the unserved branch: without that, an outage would have become a left-out section, so this is the fail-closed reading and it is pinned.
- **The root's gates. Unchanged, right.** Step 2 is not in the diff; the existing real-kernel case (a root the caller may not read answers as `get_record` does, pack unnamed) stays green on both doors.
- **`queryableFieldsOf` on both doors. Right, and not looser than plugin-security.** Both doors return the `security` service's own `getQueryableFields(object, caller)`: `/mcp` with the request's `ec`, stdio with `resolvePrincipal()`, each the same context its `fieldVisibilityOf` already uses, and stdio hands the real service through (`plugin.ts` `securityReads`). The executor admits a name only when it is in that answer AND in the caller's served schema (`served.has(n) && queryable.has(n)`), so the door can only narrow the service's answer. `undefined` falls to the contract's fallback; a throw drops the section and states it. The fields the fallback refused and the service admits are exactly masked fields whose rule is lifted for this caller, which the engine guard does not refuse either (the contract says the answer is "the exact complement of the fields those guards refuse"). The engine guard still stands behind both doors' `query`, so an over-wide answer would refuse the call, not disclose.
- **`pageCap` and the stated cut (point 14, D1's limit paragraph). Right in behaviour.** `cap = min(entry limit or row cap, pageCap - 1)`, `limit: cap + 1`, and the note carries `cap`. Both doors answer `min(OS_DATA_MAX_PAGE_SIZE, OS_DATA_QUERY_ROW_BUDGET)`, which is what the data door refuses past for an offset-0 read (`limit` over the maximum page size; `offset + limit` over the budget). A cap that is absent, `undefined`, zero or fractional changes nothing; a probe that throws fails the call. Pinned on the service and, under `OS_DATA_MAX_PAGE_SIZE=3`, on both doors with equal bytes.
- **stdio and HTTP parity for a `where` pack. Right.** `rc_filtered` (where, orderBy, limit 2) answers through `both()`; the drop for an unqueryable `where` field is pinned on both doors with the spy asserting each door asked for the same caller.
- **The spec change is prose only. Right.** One doc comment on `RecordContextNoteKind`; no schema, no `.describe()` text, no generated artifact moves.
- **`Fixes #37175`. Legitimate.** The card's What 1 to 3 and both acceptance lines landed in PR #37350; the one open half was amendment 4's `door.ts` sentence, which this diff adds, and whose behaviour #37350 already pins (`rc_vault`, `apiEnabled: false`, `notVisible` on both doors). The governing claim names this branch (7181502252) and the guard is green.

S1 (should-fix) — `Clause-②: no` is exact for the behaviour changes and inexact for `pageCap`. Refuse to left-out, and the doors' queryable answer, pull the code back to a contract ADR-0160 already declares, and a runtime permission change is outside clause ② by the seat's own negative boundary; the `no` cites the ADR section, as required. `pageCap?()` is a new optional member on `RecordContextDoor`, a type the package exports from its entry point, and `StdioDataBridgeDeps.security` gains an optional method: that enlarges a published surface. The nearest precedent, #35137 (the new optional `McpDataBridge.fieldVisibilityOf`), declared `yes (widening)`. Direction ruled here: widening, by one optional member. The level is `patch` either way, no gate reads the arm for a non-breaking change, and the at-tier review a `yes` owes is this record, so it does not fail the head; correct both declaration lines at the next touch of the changeset, or have the seat's ACCEPT record why `no` stands.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/service-record-context`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/spec` is right: a fix under existing ADR text, no authorable key, value or metadata type, so `Metadata-protocol: none` holds and takes `patch`; a widening by one optional TypeScript member also ships `patch`. The changeset body carries both declaration lines and describes all four behaviours, the new member included. `Clause-②:` see S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Security-touching.** The diff changes what a permission-narrowed caller receives on a read path. The maintainer's word for it is the first amendment of ADR-0160 (point 2). Nothing here widens a read: every row still arrives through the caller's own `get` and `query`.
- **Dev open question (which way for `Fixes #37175`): answered.** Option A was taken (re-claim 7181502252); guard green.
- **Dev flag, N5 authoring lint: escalated to the seat.** `validateAiContext` warns `ai-context-field-unknown` ("the list is left out of every answer") for `orderBy: created_at`, while the executor and both doors read the list (pinned here). An author is told the opposite of what runs. It is outside this diff and has no carrier yet; file it before #37361 closes.
- **Dev flag, disabled-package child answers `PERMISSION_DENIED`, not `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`: accepted.** Point 12: every object-level refusal carries one code. The card's acceptance line names the case.
- **Dev flag, `.describe()` texts still say "row cap": see N3.**
- **Dev flag, stdio reads plan no read window: noted.** For `get_record_context` both doors now cut at the same row. Other stdio reads are not this PR's.
- **Dev deviation, `origin/main` not merged before the PR: accepted.** CI ran on the merge ref; `mergeable_state` is clean.
- **A third door.** `pageCap` is optional, so the product-registry door (row 9, cloud#4978) still cuts or refuses unstated until it reports a cap. For the seat to carry to that row.
- **SQL push-down.** No new id materialisation and no in-app join: each related list is still one capped query with the filter, order and limit inside it.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts` holds against its implementing code: `related_truncated` fires at `limit`, at the row cap, or under the door's cap, which is what the executor does and what D3's "Every cut is stated" sentence lists. The implementing files agree with ADR-0160 D3 and D4 as read in ①.

S2 (should-fix) — the direction a disclosure would ride is not pinned on the real kernel. The harness has one caller, who holds `rc_unmask`; no case shows a masked field whose rule is NOT lifted dropping the section with the statement on both doors. Reading shows it holds (the service leaves the field out; the engine guard refuses behind it), and the spy case covers "narrower than the fallback" only by altering the service's answer. Add a second caller without the capability to `rc_unmasked_order`.

S3 (should-fix) — the `door.ts` sentence that closes #37175 cites "(ADR-0160 D3, amendment 4)". ADR-0160 has a first, second and third amendment and no fourth; "amendment 4" is item 4 of card #37175's own amendment comment (7151678330), and the harness beside it says "[card amendment 4]". The citation ships in the package's `.d.ts`. Cite D3 "Object level" (its last paragraph: a lookup whose target the caller may not read is left unexpanded) or the card.

N1 (nit) — a `related[].object` that names no object at all now passes API exposure on both doors (no declaration, nothing to refuse), is not served, and is left out with `not_visible` for every caller, an admin included; before, it refused. The executor cannot tell the two apart without the read D3 forbids, and equal answers are the ADR-0106 rule, so this is the safe reading; it is not pinned, and it turns one author defect from a first-call refusal into a statement that reads as a permission.

N2 (nit) — D1 says a door with a lower page cap "cuts the list at that cap"; the list is cut one row under it, to keep the probe row. A door cap of 1 gives an empty list with "more rows than the 0 given". Stated in the changeset and the docblock; an ADR bookkeeping line for the landing seat.

N3 (nit) — `RecordContextRelatedListSchema` `rows` and `truncated` `.describe()` texts still say "row cap". They are the texts a model reads in the tool's output schema, and they have been short since `limit` landed (#37354). Outside N1's prose-only line; needs a carrier.

N4 (nit) — `recordContextPageCap()` is written twice, byte for byte bar indentation (`domains/mcp.ts`, `stdio-data-bridge.ts`), beside `deleteRecordsCap` in `mcp-http-tools.ts`, which computes the same minimum. Parity between the doors rests on two copies staying equal; one export in `@objectstack/types` would hold it.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37361-left-out-queryable-doors`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `a50181d4e7`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5: the three should-fix findings of contract record 7181694279 are fixed in this PR before landing. The rest of L1 reads clean.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 8 files (+483/−44), `Fixes #37361` and `Fixes #37175`. The second closes legitimately: the `door.ts` sentence was #37175's only open half, and re-claim 7181502252 names this branch. `l1-face` flagged `keywords-other-cards`, which is intended. It also flagged the PR-body guard, which was red at 02:37Z and is green at 03:15Z after the re-claim.
2. **Premise**: per the record, a child the caller is not served is left out and stated, and nothing leaks: no section, row, count or field name. The root's gates still refuse the whole call. Both doors return the security service's own `getQueryableFields` and are never looser than plugin-security. `pageCap` cuts are stated. stdio/HTTP `where` parity is pinned.
3. **Owed in this PR**:
   - S1: `pageCap` adds an optional member to the exported `RecordContextDoor`, which enlarges a published surface. Declare `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the PR body and the changeset; precedent #35137. The level stays `patch`.
   - S2: add a real-kernel pin on both doors showing that a masked field whose rule is not lifted for the caller drops the section. The harness's one caller holds `rc_unmask`.
   - S3: the `door.ts` sentence cites "(ADR-0160 D3, amendment 4)", but ADR-0160 has no fourth amendment, and the citation ships in the `.d.ts`. Cite D3, or the card comment 7151678330 item 4.
   The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations**: contract nits N1 (an unknown `related[].object` is now left out, unpinned), N2 (the cut lands one row under the door cap, an ADR D1 bookkeeping line), N3 (the `rows`/`truncated` describes still say "row cap") and N4 (`recordContextPageCap()` is duplicated). N3 and N4 may ride along with the fix.
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: the `validateAiContext` warning that an `orderBy: created_at` list "is left out" contradicts the executor. That goes to #37415.
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned, default tier, `Security-touching: yes`. A same-head at-tier PASS with S1–S3 closed is owed, then **ACCEPT**. The area lands it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `88a1447c951570e533ee1cb7c4b21be8e44a5f53`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts + packages/types/src/query-read-limits.ts, packages/types/src/query-read-limits.test.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/door.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/runtime/src/mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts, content/docs/references/ai/record-context-tools.mdx, .changeset/37361-record-context-left-out-queryable-doors.md
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Delta review of PR #37412 (cards #37361 and #37175) after its rework: one commit, `88a1447c`, on `a50181d4e`, the head record 7181694279 reviewed. Read-only: the delta diff (9 files, +132/-58), the PR body as it stands, the #37361 comments after that record (claim amendments 7181717837 and 7183121810, delta report 7183101611), and the check-runs on this head. `record-context-tools.ts` and its service test are byte-identical to the reviewed head, so every judgment of the first record on the executor stands and is not repeated.

Check-runs on the head: 62 success, 12 skipped, 0 failure. `PR-body guards` and `Check Changeset` are green on both of their runs (04:30Z and 04:31Z); `Check PR Size` and `Auto Label` read skipped on the 04:31 re-run and were green at 04:30. `mergeable_state` is clean.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`resolveQueryReadPageCap()`, a new export of `@objectstack/types`. Right, and declared.** It reaches the package entry through `export * from './query-read-limits.js'`. Its body is the removed door-local function, word for word: the smaller of `maxPageSize` and `rowBudget` from `resolveQueryReadLimits(env)`, `undefined` when neither is set, and it throws on an unreadable value as that function does. Four unit cases pin unset, one set, both set in either order, and the throw. The changeset names it twice (the surface sentence and its own bullet), the PR body names it under S1, and `@objectstack/types` takes a `patch` entry, so the widening declaration covers it. Claim amendment 7183121810 adds the file, its test and the changeset entry to the surface: fenced.
- **Both doors answer `pageCap` from that one function. Right.** The two local copies are deleted and nothing else in either door moves; the real-kernel case under `OS_DATA_MAX_PAGE_SIZE=3` is unchanged and green, so the cut is the same row as on the reviewed head.
- **The `rows` and `truncated` descriptions of a related list. Right.** They are text in the tool's output schema and change no accepted or produced shape. Both now say what the executor does: up to the entry's `limit`, else the row cap, or fewer under the door's page cap. The reference page moved with them in both of its tables and no other generated artifact did; the generated-artifact gates are green. Fenced by claim amendment 7181717837.
- **The second caller in the real-kernel harness. Right.** `rc_unmask` left the baseline set and sits in `rc_unmasker`, granted to `usr_member` alone through a `sys_user_permission_set` answer that the real `resolveAuthzContext` resolves. The case asserts its own preconditions first: the two contexts differ in the capability, the real service lists `serial` as queryable for one and not the other, and the stdio door's root read carried `usr_plain`. The earlier cases still run as `usr_member`, and the case that needs the capability asserts the caller holds it.

S1: closed. The PR body and the changeset both read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` at line start, with `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset lists the three additions: `RecordContextDoor.pageCap?()`, the optional `getQueryableFields` on `StdioDataBridgeDeps.security`, and `resolveQueryReadPageCap`. Claim amendment 7181717837 carries the corrected line.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on five packages is right: the widening is non-protocol (optional TypeScript members and one function), which ships `patch`, and `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`. `@objectstack/types` is in the changeset because it now publishes the new export; `@objectstack/spec` stays in for the doc line and the two descriptions.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Security-touching, unchanged.** The rework adds no read and changes no gate; its one production change is where the page cap is computed.
- **Dev deviation, the types surface was outside amendment 7181717837 when the commit was made: answered.** Amendment 7183121810 records it, after the report.
- **Dev deviation, `origin/main` not merged: accepted.** CI ran on the merge ref and the PR merges clean.
- **N5 of the card (the `validateAiContext` warning on `orderBy: created_at`): carried.** The report names #37415 as its carrier. The first record's escalation is answered.
- **Dev note, the harness names the key's owner per call through its proxy: accepted.** It is how one stdio session reads as two users; the case proves the stdio read's context before it trusts the answer.
- **SQL push-down.** Nothing new: no id materialisation and no in-app join in the delta.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts` holds against the executor: the three places a list is cut are the three the two descriptions and the `related_truncated` doc line name. `packages/types/src/query-read-limits.ts` holds against the data door it describes: an offset-0 read is refused past the maximum page size or past the row budget, so the smaller is the most such a read may ask for.

S2: closed. The direction a disclosure would ride is now pinned on the real kernel, on both doors with equal bytes: as `usr_plain`, the pack ordered by the masked `serial` answers without error, with no `related` member, one `not_visible` note with no `object`, and none of `rc_step`, the quoted field name, a serial value or a row name in the text. The control leg in the same case reads the four rows in serial order as `usr_member`. The reported ablation (`&&` to `||` in the queryable check) turned this case into a whole-call refusal by the engine guard, which is the fail-closed backstop the first record read.

S3: closed. The `door.ts` sentence cites `ADR-0160 D3 "Object level"`, the section whose last paragraph says a lookup whose target the caller may not read is left unexpanded.

N3: closed. See ①.

N4: closed. See ①. `deleteRecordsCap` keeps its own minimum against its 200-row constant, which is a different number and is left alone.

N1 (nit) — open, unchanged. A `related[].object` that names no object is left out with `not_visible` for every caller. Still unpinned.

N2 (nit) — open, unchanged. ADR-0160 D1 says a door "cuts the list at that cap"; the list is cut one row under it. An ADR bookkeeping line for the landing seat.

N5 (nit) — new. The seat note that closes the PR body still says "Final-head readings (a50181d4e) are in the os-dev report 7181466841". The body's own readings are at `88a1447c9` and the final-head report is 7183101611. The note is the seat's to correct.

Head-sha: `88a1447c951570e533ee1cb7c4b21be8e44a5f53`
